digest.component_or_area: Jira Reconciler baseline advance and inbound field sync
propositions: A local status change is silently reverted by the reconciler when the baseline snapshot lags the outbound push by one pass, because the baseline is advanced from the pre-push snapshot rather than the last-synced value

The baseline-to-local equality check in _suppressed_by_inbound loses its premise for one pass after rebar itself pushes a status, making an operator reopen (revert to prior value) indistinguishable from unchanged local, so inbound overwrites it

Status transitions can soft-fail (no legal reverse transition, caught by backstop at applier.py:725-726) while the pass still exits 0, so the baseline must advance only on per-mutation success, not on pass exit code

The defect affects all five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) because they share the _suppressed_by_inbound guard, but status changes are the most exposed because reopen and un-claim are exactly the ABA-vulnerable shape

ADR 0026 mandates direction-preservation regression cells but they existed only for title; the status cell drove an unused adapter path, leaving status never pinned on the live diff_canonical_fields path where the bug hid
